source_rfp: Service Logic - Field Service Management Platform RFP (Version E, 2026-06-02)
source_instrument: Service Logic FSM RFP - Vendor Scorecard v1.xlsx
note: The headline score is now a decision-weighted score. It starts with requirement evidence, then applies confidence discounts, architecture caps, project/job-cost ownership penalties, implementation risk, evidence quality, agentic/data-platform upside, and commercial viability. The Section 30 OOB capability lens remains visible as a separate confidence-adjusted functional view.

categories.name: Operating fit
categories.good_looks_like: Service Logic work-to-cash, technician adoption, OpCo onboarding, governance, compliance, and customer experience evidence.

categories.name: Project/job-cost control
categories.good_looks_like: How much of project execution, WIP, AIA/retainage, certified payroll, and job-cost ownership lives in the FSM workflow instead of being pushed to ERP/add-ons.

categories.name: Enterprise architecture, security & scale
categories.good_looks_like: North Star platform fit: single-enterprise operating model, security, scale, tenancy, integration posture, data access, and resilience.

categories.name: Implementation certainty & accountability
categories.good_looks_like: Clarity that the vendor can deliver the promised model without a year of open-ended configuration, custom work, or unclear partner handoffs.

categories.name: Evidence quality & transparency
categories.good_looks_like: How credible, specific, and transparent the response and call color were, including whether caveats were surfaced honestly.

categories.name: Agentic/data platform future
categories.good_looks_like: Openness, AI/data architecture, and ability to support future agentic workflows beyond today's shipped features.

categories.name: Commercial/vendor viability
categories.good_looks_like: Scale, stability, commercial fit, and vendor viability for a 40-plus OpCo HVAC rollup.

quality_scale.5: Excellent: proven out-of-the-box or already-productized capability with strong evidence and low delivery risk.
quality_scale.4: Good: standard configuration or proven template with clear ownership and credible implementation path.
quality_scale.3: Adequate: meets the need, but proof, configuration effort, or accountability must be validated.
quality_scale.2: Weak: materially dependent on custom work, partner/add-on delivery, ERP assumptions, or thin evidence.
quality_scale.1: Poor: gap, roadmap, unsupported claim, or failure against a non-negotiable decision screen.

met_values.Partial: Partially provided; some aspects unmet or need work.
met_values.No: Not provided and no acceptable path to it.

response_codes.OOB: Out of the box - fully supported in current GA release, no modifications.
response_codes.CONFIG: Configurable via admin configuration, no code changes.
response_codes.EXTENSION: Built using the product's extensible framework.
response_codes.CUSTOM: Custom development - scripting or code-level changes required.
response_codes.PARTNER: Delivered via certified third-party / ISV / marketplace partner.
response_codes.ROADMAP: Planned / not yet available; published future release.
response_codes.GAP: Not supported and no published roadmap.

moscow.Must: Non-negotiable. A 'No', GAP, or ROADMAP on any Must is a basis for disqualification. A Must answered CUSTOM meets the requirement (delivered via custom development) — it does not disqualify, but heavy reliance on custom work is a risk to flag.
moscow.Should: High priority; expected of a market-leading platform. Absence hurts scoring.
moscow.Could: Desirable differentiator; not required for initial deployment.
moscow.Won't: Explicitly out of scope; no response required.

gating_rules.description: Must-level gaps still matter, but the revised score also applies explicit decision caps. A North Star architecture failure can cap a vendor below the finalist range even when many functional rows are marked Yes. Project/job-cost ownership, implementation accountability, and add-on/ERP dependency can materially discount otherwise complete responses.

raise: Concrete evidence cited (references, screenshots, named customers)
lower: Capability must be validated in live demo (Appendix F)

confidence_model.rule: Every score is confidence-adjusted. OOB/proven capability can receive full credit; standard configuration receives partial credit; custom, partner, add-on, ERP-dependent, roadmap, or vague claims receive escalating discounts. The call transcript is used to resolve ties and apply caps where row-level matrices are identical.

category_rationale.operating: Blends confidence-adjusted W2C, TPA, ACQ, EVG, RLC, and CXR evidence rather than raw yes/config row counts.
category_rationale.project: Separates project/job-cost control owned in FSM from ERP, add-on, partner, or roadmap dependency.
category_rationale.architecture: Reflects the North Star architecture screen, including tenancy, scale, security, integration, and data access.
category_rationale.implementation: Discounts theoretical configurability when delivery ownership, partner accountability, or implementation duration is uncertain.
category_rationale.evidence: Credits response transparency, specificity, and proof while penalizing vague or overly interpretive answers.
category_rationale.agentic: Uses the agentic/data-platform read, weighted for data openness and AI capability.
category_rationale.commercial: Captures vendor stability, scale, and commercial fit for the Service Logic portfolio.

gate.summary: Passes the decision gate. No architecture cap; validate project-financial specifics in demo and references.
Conditional pass. Enterprise architecture and scale clear the platform screen, but configuration burden, demo proof, and partner accountability must be resolved.

architectural_gate_flags: Project/job-cost ownership appears materially dependent on ERP/add-on boundaries and must be proved.
gate.summary: Conditional pass with material concern. The architecture is not the same hard failure as BuildOps/ServiceTitan, but project-control ownership and add-on dependency materially reduce the score.

unmet_musts.reason: North Star architecture, integration, and security posture not proven for the required enterprise operating model.

architectural_gate_flags: Architecture/integration/security had too many gap or roadmap responses for the target operating model.
gate.summary: Do not advance. ServiceTitan gets credit for response transparency and market fit, but fails the North Star architecture screen.

unmet_musts.reason: North Star architecture and single-enterprise operating model not proven.

architectural_gate_flags: Architecture and response credibility do not support the required enterprise-scale operating model.
gate.summary: Do not advance. BuildOps has useful operating coverage, but the architecture screen and response-confidence discount cap the decision score.
